To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angiotensin AT2 receptor stimulates ERK in quescent but inhibits NGF-stimulating ERK in PC12W neuronal cells.
angiotensin AT2 receptors inhibit ERK in NGFF-stimulated PC 12W cells.
the ANG II type 2 receptor modulates ERKS activity, depending on the overall input to the ERK pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiotensins in neuronal development and differentiation.
the role of the AT(2)-receptor in the differentiation of the PC12W cell line.
the influence of the AT(2)-receptor on the activity of ERKI and ERKII and its potential role in the process of neuronal differentiation of PC12W cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT(1) and AT(2) receptors have different effects on the ERK1 and/or ERK2 pathway, which are dependent on the cellular state and the presence of other growth factors.
the AT(1) and AT(2) receptors are not only involved in neuronal differentiation but also in the modulation of the ERK pathway.
AT(2) receptors are involved in the regulation of ERK activity, which is dependent on the cellular input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AT(2) receptors modulate the NGF-mediated differentiation of PC12 cells by inhibiting the activity of ER via the MEK/ERK cascade.
the AT(1) and AT(2) receptors exert different effects on ERK1/2 activation and that these differences are reflected in the regulation of neurite outgrowth.
ANG II is a modulatory factor in the process of neuronal differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AT(1) and AT(2) receptors have opposite actions on the ERK1 and 2 pathway in PC12W neurons.
the angiotensin AT2 receptor modulates ER kinase activity in PC12 cells depending on the cellular context, i.e., in quiescent or nerve growth factor (NGF)-stimulated cells.
the ERK pathway is regulated by the AT2 receptor in a manner that is dependent on cellular input.
